author: dashpole
content: model/textparse: follow-up improvements and spec validations for OpenMetrics 2.0 parser Follow-up tracking issue to address the remaining open review comments from https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606, just to make sure it doesn't get lost. ### Bug Fixes & Parser Options #### 1. Unescape exemplar label names with `unreplace` - [ ] Unescape exemplar label names in `parseSingleExemplar` ([discussion](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3812976624)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L602-L611 From @dashpole: > ```suggestion > p.builder.Add(unreplace(string(p.l.b[a:b])), unreplace(string(p.l.b[c:d]))) > ``` > Label names can contain escape sequences in OM2, so we should unescape the name with `unreplace` here like in `Labels()`. --- #### 2. Consume null bytes inside exemplar label values (`sEValue`) - [ ] Include `sEValue` in `openMetrics2Lexer.next()` null-byte check ([discussion](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3758085497)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L60-L68 From @dashpole: > Should `sEValue` also be included in this check so null bytes inside exemplar label values are consumed properly? --- #### 3. Retain and handle `opts.IgnoreNativeHistograms` - [ ] Respect `opts.IgnoreNativeHistograms` in `OpenMetrics2Parser` when parsing composite histograms ([discussion](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3758085591)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L161-L168 From @dashpole: > Looks like `opts.IgnoreNativeHistograms` is not retained or handled in `OpenMetrics2Parser` when parsing composite histograms. --- #### 4. Unexport `OpenMetrics2Parser` - [ ] Make `OpenMetrics2Parser` private (`openMetrics2Parser`) to match `openMetricsParser` and `promParser` ([discussion](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3468043588)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L100-L103 From @dashpole: > does this type actually need to be exported? I don't think we export `openMetricsParser` or `promParser`. From @bwplotka: > We can keep it private for now, up to us --- ### Spec Validation & Input Hardening #### 5. Reject empty quoted label names in `parseLVals` - [ ] Check `curTStart == curTI` after stripping quotes so empty label names like `{""="val"}` are rejected ([discussion 1](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3812976794), [discussion 2](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3758085406)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L692-L699 From @dashpole: > If `curTStart == curTI` after trimming quotes, empty label names like `{""="val"}` are currently accepted. Per the OM2 ABNF (`escaped-string-non-empty`), should we reject empty label names here like we do for metric names? --- #### 6. Validate non-negative `zero_count` and non-gauge `count` in `buildNativeHistogram` - [ ] Validate `zeroCount >= 0` (and `count >= 0` for non-gauge histograms) before casting to `uint64` ([discussion 1](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3812976922), [discussion 2](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3758085298)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L969-L975 https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L1032-L1037 From @dashpole: > If `zero_count` or non-gauge `count` is negative, casting to `uint64` in `buildNativeHistogram` wraps around to `maxUint64`. We should validate that `zeroCount >= 0` (and `count >= 0` for non-gauges) similar to `zero_threshold`. --- #### 7. Validate classic histogram `le` bucket thresholds and allow `-Inf` in `parseBuckets` - [ ] Return an error if `le` fails `strconv.ParseFloat` or is `NaN`, and allow `-Inf` as the first bucket threshold ([discussion 1](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3812977043), [discussion 2](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3758085103)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L1411-L1439 From @dashpole: > If `le` is not a valid float (or `NaN`), the parsing error is ignored and the invalid threshold is yielded. Also, initializing `prevLe` to `math.Inf(-1)` causes valid `-Inf` bucket thresholds permitted by OM2 ABNF (`ch-neg-inf-bucket`) to be rejected by the `<=` check. --- #### 8. Validate summary `quantile` values in `parseQuantiles` - [ ] Return an error when `q` is non-numeric, `NaN`, or outside `[0.0, 1.0]` ([discussion 1](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3812977165), [discussion 2](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3758085203)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L1480-L1491 From @dashpole: > If `q` is not a valid float or `NaN`, `strconv.ParseFloat` error is ignored and the invalid quantile string is yielded without validation. Should we check the error and verify `0 <= qf && qf <= 1`? --- #### 9. Validate empty `UNIT` for `info` and `stateset` metric families - [ ] Reject non-empty unit metadata when metric type is `info` or `stateset` ([discussion](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3561743599)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L400-L405 From @dashpole: > OM2 spec requires Info and StateSet metric families to have an empty unit string (`MetricFamilies of Type Info/StateSets MUST have an empty Unit string.`). Should we validate `p.unit == ""` when `p.mtype` is `info` or `stateset`? --- #### 10. Validate `info` metric family `_info` suffix and sample value `1` - [ ] Validate that `info` MetricFamily names end with `_info` and have sample value `1` ([discussion](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3561743605)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L381-L384 https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L486-L493 From @dashpole: > OM2 spec requires Info family names to end in `_info` (`The MetricFamily name for Info metrics MUST end in _info.`) and sample values to equal `1` (`The Sample value MUST always be 1.`). Should we validate the `_info` suffix and sample value `1` for info metrics? --- #### 11. Decide whether to reject `\r` carriage returns in line endings - [ ] Confirm whether `\r` should be explicitly rejected or tolerated ([discussion](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3561743596)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L329-L337 From @dashpole: > OM2 spec requires line endings to be `\n` without carriage returns (`Line endings MUST be signalled with line feed (\n) and MUST NOT contain carriage returns (\r).`). Should we explicitly reject inputs containing `\r`? From @bwplotka: > Yea, good question. Here is where we could be relaxed a bit --- ### Performance, Allocations & Field Ordering #### 12. Avoid map/slice allocations and enforce composite field ordering - [ ] Replace `kvMap` allocations with byte-offset/slice parsing so composite field order from the spec can also be asserted, and avoid intermediate allocations in `parseIntBuckets` / `parseFloatBuckets` ([discussion 1](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3163175574), [discussion 2](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3579516693), [discussion 3](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3163193132), [discussion 4](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3163193977)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L748-L771 https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L1123-L1135 https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L1151-L1163 From @dashpole: > We probably want to avoid allocating a new map for every composite value we parse. > > I think this would look something like [parseLVals](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/16034ecf3b7cc5da96a1f0c324d0eed927267877/model/textparse/promparse.go#L406) in promparse.go, which also parses a bracketed, comma-separated structure. It appends the "offsets" into a pre-allocated slice, where offsets are pointers into the byte buffer. > > The rest of the parsing code just operates on `[]bytes`, using functions from the `bytes` package (e.g. `bytes.Equal`) instead of the string equivalents, and using yoloString when we need to (e.g. to call strconv.ParseFloat) From @krajorama: > Unfortunately this map makes it impossible to assert the order of fields dictated by the spec. So that's another point in favor of David's suggestion in https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606/changes#r3163175574 From @dashpole (on `parseIntBuckets` and `parseFloatBuckets`): > This allocates as well. We should avoid this if we can. See my comment above. --- ### Documentation & Benchmark Testdata #### 13. Fix classic histogram bucket order in `parseHistogramComposite` doc comment and cover `_total`-less counter in benchmark testdata - [ ] Update doc comment example on `parseHistogramComposite` so `+Inf` is last ([discussion](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3579477524)) - [ ] Include a counter omitting the `_total` suffix in `alltypes.bench.om2.txt` ([discussion](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18606#discussion_r3418693020)) https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/openmetrics2parse.go#L835 From @krajorama: > nit: > ```suggestion > // {count:12,sum:5.5,bucket:[1.0:3,2.0:7,+Inf:12]} > ``` https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ffe0b67b8156d0fa815055a80adbc757b68c63e3/model/textparse/testdata/alltypes.bench.om2.txt#L38-L40 From @krajorama: > OM2.0 allows you to omit the suffix as well > ```suggestion > jobs_completed 18234.0 1710000000.0 > ```

author: Suhail98
content: I'd like to pick up the numeric validation items — 6, 7 and 8. They are the same shape of bug (a dropped `ParseFloat` error or a missing range check) and they all sit in the composite value parsing path, so they read well as one change: - **6**: the integer path is taken whenever `count`/`zero_count` are integral, so a negative value like `-5` reaches `uint64(count)` and lands as `18446744073709551611`. `isGauge` does not affect the float/int decision, so `gcount` hits the same cast — I would validate both unless you would rather keep gauges out of scope here. - **7**: besides the ignored error, a `NaN` threshold passes the `lef <= prevLe` check (every NaN comparison is false) and then becomes `prevLe`, which silently disables the ordering check for the rest of the buckets. And `-Inf` as the first threshold per `ch-neg-inf-bucket`. - **8**: same dropped error for `q`, plus the `[0.0, 1.0]` bound. I will add cases to the existing table tests and leave the rest of the list alone, in particular 12. Happy to re-scope if any of these are already in flight.

author: bwplotka
content:
Proposal: Metadata manipulation — let users fix a metric's type, unit and help ### TL;DR Prometheus lets operators rewrite **labels** freely (`metric_relabel_configs`, `write_relabel_configs`), but gives them **no supported way to rewrite metadata** — `TYPE`, `UNIT`, `HELP`. Metadata is whatever the target or sender said it was, forever. That was tolerable while metadata was decorative. We are slowly in the world where it no longer is: with [PROM-39](https://github.com/prometheus/proposals/blob/main/proposals/2024-09-25_metadata-labels.md) / `--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels`, type and unit are part of series identity, selectable in PromQL, [drive `rate()` counter-ness annotations](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/10f69629039e0215d056eb4948f0bd0fd22f5c89/promql/engine.go#L2445-L2462), and are necessary for downstream systems e.g. OpenTelemetry and Google. **Wrong metadata could be now assumed as actively harmful, and users cannot fix it in Prometheus.** This issue is primarily a **collection of use cases** to see if we have some consensus to add such mechanism to Prometheus (or other use cases I am missing). Proper proposal should be done, but I wanted to gather feedback first. ## Use cases ### 1. Specifying a missing or wrong type, unit or help ##### Example: The exporter miss `# TYPE` (or says `untyped`) A large share of exposition in the wild is untyped: textfile collector output, `statsd_exporter`, JMX exporter, home-grown `/metrics` handlers, legacy vendor agents. ``` # HELP myapp_requests_total Total requests. myapp_requests_total{route="/api"} 4213 ``` The operator knows well this is a counter. They cannot patch the exporter (third party, vendored, or 200 teams own it). With type-aware PromQL UX they now get warned — or silently degraded — forever on metrics they don't own. > **Wants:** "for this job, anything matching `myapp_.*_total` is a counter." ##### Example: No `# UNIT` (impossible in Prometheus text format anyway) The name encodes milliseconds. The operator wants `__unit__="milliseconds"` so unit-aware UI formatting and future unit-aware functions work. The inverse also happens: an exporter declares a misleading unit that the operator wants to strip. ``` # TYPE http_request_latency_ms gauge http_request_latency_ms 12.5 ``` > **Wants:** derive `__unit__` from a name suffix, or set/clear it outright. ##### Example: RW/OTLP parity metadata fixed on RW or OTLP receive OTel users have the Collector `transform` processor: ```yaml transform: metric_statements: - set(metric.unit, "s") where metric.name == "foo" - set(metric.description, "") ``` Pushing OTLP **directly** to Prometheus loses this entirely: `OTLPConfig` exposes nine fixed knobs and no transform hook. Users end up deploying a whole Collector purely to fix a unit string. > **Wants:** the same metadata fixes available on the OTLP and RW receive path. ### 2. Do certain relabelling based on type, unit ##### Example: Rename all __type__==counter without _total suffix to have _total suffix. > **Wants:** perform relabel action based on metadata Today this **silently drops the metadata** — the family match is done against the post-relabel name. If we let users rename, we should let them restate the metadata that goes with the new name. > **Wants:** rename and metadata stay consistent, or can be re-declared in the same block. ### 3. Dropping huge `HELP` strings Real-world exporters ship multi-kilobyte `HELP` text: whole paragraphs, embedded JSON, even stack traces. That costs head memory, WAL bytes, and Remote Write 2.0 bandwidth — repeated per series. There is no knob for this today short of all-or-nothing `metadata_config.send: false` (RW1 only), which also throws away type and unit. > **Wants:** "drop HELP for this job" / "truncate HELP to N bytes" / "drop HELP only for these metrics."

Current state — two unsynchronized metadata channels (click to expand)

 There are **two parallel metadata channels**, and one of them is *already user-mutable, by accident*: | | Channel 1: `metadata.Metadata` record | Channel 2: `__type__` / `__unit__` labels | |---|---|---| | Keyed by | metric **family** name | **series** label set | | Source | `# TYPE/# UNIT/# HELP`, RW2 `Metadata`, OTLP descriptor | parsers, gated on `type-and-unit-labels` | | Carries HELP | yes | **no** | | Reaches | metadata WAL records, RW2 `Metadata`, `/api/v1/metadata` | TSDB series labels, PromQL, RW2 type+unit | | Mutable by user | **no** | **yes, undocumented** | **Findings:** 1. **Relabeling of `__type__`/`__unit__` already works, undocumented.** Parsers inject the labels ([`promparse.go#L250`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/model/textparse/promparse.go#L250)), relabeling runs *after* that ([`scrape_append_v2.go#L224`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/scrape/scrape_append_v2.go#L224)), and nothing strips `__`-prefixed labels on the sample path — the `__meta_*` strip at [`target.go#L691-L697`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/scrape/target.go#L691-L697) is target-relabeling only. There is a merged test asserting exactly this, `TestTypeUnitReLabel` ([`scrape_test.go#L6937`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/scrape/scrape_test.go#L6937), from #16738/#16743) — and it passes **without** `EnableTypeAndUnitLabels`. 2. **The docs say the opposite.** [`feature_flags.md#L253`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/docs/feature_flags.md#L253): *"All the user provided labels with `__type__` and `__unit__` will be overridden."* True only for **exposition**-provided labels, which the parsers drop; not for relabel-provided ones, which run later and win. 3. **The metadata record never sees the relabeling.** [`scrape_append_v2.go#L312-L323`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/scrape/scrape_append_v2.go#L312-L323) (v1: [`scrape.go#L2047-L2060`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/scrape/scrape.go#L2047-L2060)) attaches `lastMeta` straight from the parser. After a relabel, series labels, the metadata WAL record, and `/api/v1/metadata` can all disagree. 4. **Renaming silently drops metadata** (use case 3): `isSeriesPartOfFamily(lset.Get(__name__), lastMFName, ...)` is evaluated on the **post-relabel** name ([`scrape_append_v2.go#L315`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/scrape/scrape_append_v2.go#L315)), so the family match fails. 5. **Send and receive have opposite precedence.** Sender: labels win ([`queue_manager.go#L1975-L2001`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/storage/remote/queue_manager.go#L1975-L2001)). Receiver: the record wins and **overwrites incoming labels** ([`write_handler.go#L327-L339`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/storage/remote/write_handler.go#L327-L339)). So metadata edits don't reliably round-trip a RW2 hop. 6. **`HELP` has no label form** and is explicitly zeroed on the label path ([`queue_manager.go#L1984`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/storage/remote/queue_manager.go#L1984)). No way to set, rewrite or drop it (use case 4). 7. **No hook on OTLP or RW receive** (use cases 6, 7): `OTLPConfig` has fixed knobs only ([`config.go#L1771-L1789`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/config/config.go#L1771-L1789)); the RW handler has no relabeling. 8. **Unit values are unvalidated** and inconsistently normalized between label and record on the OTLP path — UTF-8-aware `UnitNamer` at [`helper.go#L165-L173`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/storage/remote/otlptranslator/prometheusremotewrite/helper.go#L165-L173) vs. non-UTF-8 at [`metrics_to_prw.go#L241`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/storage/remote/otlptranslator/prometheusremotewrite/metrics_to_prw.go#L241). See the TODO at [`schema/labels.go#L62-L65`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/schema/labels.go#L62-L65). > [!IMPORTANT] > Findings 1 and 2 mean we already ship an undocumented behaviour that users may depend on, and finding 5 means it doesn't round-trip. Even deciding *"we don't want metadata manipulation"* requires a spec and doc fix here.

Open questions (click to expand)

 - **Scope**: scrape only, or also the OTLP endpoint and the RW receiver? (Use cases 6 and 7 say all three.) - **Family vs. series semantics**: what happens when sibling series of one family get different `__type__`? - **`__help__`**: write-only relabel target, or a real label dropped before storage? It must never become identifying. - **Precedence**, definitively: labels vs. records, on send *and* receive — today they disagree (finding 5). - **Validation**: reject unknown type values at config load? At runtime? With what metric or annotation? - **Flag gating**: should metadata manipulation require `type-and-unit-labels`? Note relabeling `__type__` works *without* it today. - **Interaction with `metadata-wal-records`**, and with the metadata API, which reads the *scrape cache* rather than TSDB. - **Suffix conventions**: if a user sets `__unit__=seconds` on `foo_milliseconds`, do we warn? Rename? Neither? - **Removal semantics**: is `__type__=unknown` / `__unit__=""` the way to delete metadata? - **Agent mode**, which currently drops metadata entirely ([`tsdb/agent/db.go#L1093-L1094`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/tsdb/agent/db.go#L1093-L1094)).
### Related One related aspect is that renaming a metric shouldn't destroy its metadata. Also when you drop metrics, cache preserves metadata. This has to be fixed first. * https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17864 and https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/19555 for recording rules. - #16610 — `[meta] PROM-39 type-and-unit-labels stability` (open) — natural parent for this work. - #16738 / #16743 — `PROM-39: Add tests for relabeling of type and unit labels` (closed) — closest prior art: behaviour tested, never specified or documented. - #17900 — `textparse: Move scrape.isSeriesPartOfFamily to text parser and optimize` (open) — overlaps the family-matching fragility above. - [PROM-39 proposal](https://github.com/prometheus/proposals/blob/main/proposals/2024-09-25_metadata-labels.md), including its open "More strict unit and type value definition" question.

author: bwplotka
content:
Some quick idea on how this could be possible: ### A. Specify relabeling of `__type__` / `__unit__` and special __help__ label (not propagated to label) Declare that the **effective metadata is derived from the final, post-relabel label set** (`schema.NewMetadataFromLabels`), and feed that into the metadata record, `/api/v1/metadata` and RW2. ```yaml metric_relabel_configs: - source_labels: [__name__] # use case 1 regex: "myapp_.*_total" target_label: __type__ replacement: counter - source_labels: [__name__] # use case 2 regex: ".*_milliseconds" target_label: __unit__ replacement: milliseconds - source_labels: [__name__] # drop help regex: "myapp_.*_total" target_label: __help__ action: droplabel ``` * ✅ No new config surface; composes with what users already know; half-implemented and already tested. * ✅ Supports most use cases around `__help__` `__name__` and `__type__` in the same block. * ❌ HELP is non-identifying and large; it shouldn't become a label, so it's kind of weird to have it here. * ❌ What about other native metadata one day? * ❌ **Series vs. family mismatch**: classic histogram family `foo` is `foo_bucket`/`foo_sum`/`foo_count`; a user can set `__type__` on one and not the others. Per-series records tolerate that; the family-keyed scrape cache and `/api/v1/metadata` don't. * ❌ Per-series cost; typos (`guage`) silently accepted. Needs value validation plus an invalid-metadata counter. * ❌ Doesn't reach OTLP or RW receive (use cases 6, 7) -- although we it can with https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/19675

Other ideas for a solution (click to expand)

 ### B. A family-level `metadata_relabel_configs` A second relabel stage over a *virtual* label set `{__name__, __type__, __unit__, __help__}`, run once per metric family per scrape, before `metric_relabel_configs`. ```yaml scrape_configs: - job_name: legacy-app metadata_relabel_configs: - source_labels: [__name__] regex: "myapp_.*_total" target_label: __type__ replacement: counter - target_label: __help__ # use case 4 replacement: "" ``` * ✅ Covers `HELP`; correct family-level semantics; cheap (families ≪ series); validatable at config load. * ✅ Keeps both channels in sync by construction — the record is what's rewritten, labels are derived from it. * ❌ New config surface; a second relabel stage to explain; ordering vs `metric_relabel_configs` must be specified. * ❌ OTLP and RW-receive have no "family" notion and need separate wiring. ### C. Declarative overrides instead of relabeling ```yaml metric_metadata_overrides: - match: '{__name__=~"myapp_.*_total"}' type: counter unit: seconds help: "" # explicit empty = drop ``` * ✅ Easy to read, validate and generate from a UI; no regex-capture footguns; obvious failure modes. * ✅ Could apply uniformly at scrape, OTLP and RW receive — covers every use case above. * ❌ Another matching mechanism to maintain. * ❌ Less expressive: no capture-group-driven derivation like `(.*)_seconds` → `unit=seconds`. ### D. OTTL-style transformation language Adopt an OTTL-ish statement language at all ingest points, like the Collector's `transform` processor. * ✅ One language for scrape/OTLP/RW; familiar to OTel users; extensible beyond metadata. * ❌ Very large scope: new DSL, parser, perf and safety story; Prometheus has historically resisted a second expression language. * ❌ Plausibly the right answer for "arbitrary transformation", and the wrong answer for "my exporter forgot `# TYPE`". ### E. Do nothing — document "use a Collector or a proxy exporter" * ✅ Zero maintenance. * ❌ Heavy for a one-line fix; unavailable in the pure-Prometheus scrape path; strictly worse now that type matters in PromQL. We'd still have to spec or remove the accidental behaviour in findings 1–2. ### Suggested direction **A as the specified baseline (it is already the de-facto behaviour), plus B's family-level stage for `HELP` and for keeping the record in sync:** 1. Spec and document that post-relabel `__type__`/`__unit__` are authoritative; derive the metadata record from the final label set so all outputs agree. 2. Fix rename-drops-metadata and the send/receive precedence inversion. 3. Add a `__help__` write-only relabel target at the family stage. 4. Validate type values; normalize and validate unit values, picking up the [`schema/labels.go`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/schema/labels.go#L62-L65) TODO.

author: KurodaKayn
content: My take is that A+B makes sense, with the family-level stage supplying HELP and the initial type/unit values, and metric relabeling applying any per-series overrides afterward. PROM-39 already explicitly allows modifying type and unit through `metric_relabel_configs`, so deprecating that would be a separate compatibility decision. For renames, the association with the original family's metadata would need to survive relabeling. Adding an earlier metadata stage alone wouldn't fix the lookup against the renamed metric. The less obvious part is `/api/v1/metadata`. Suppose two series from the same scraped family keep the same name, but a relabel rule changes the type on only one of them. Returning both resulting metadata variants seems preferable to picking whichever series happens to be processed first. That means the scrape cache would need to represent the results after relabeling, rather than just the original family metadata. Your link to #14013 raises a related question: should that cache also exclude a family's metadata once all its series have been dropped? A family-level pass before metric relabeling wouldn't know that yet, especially when the drop rule depends on sample labels. Would you include those cache/API changes in the A+B proposal, or handle them separately? That seems worth settling before defining how the API, WAL metadata and RW2 should agree.

author: bwplotka
content: test(textparse): Add NHCBParser test for ungrouped series This PR adds a test that documents the negative effect on NHCB parsing of scrape targets that break the OpenMetrics [interleaving](https://prometheus.io/docs/specs/om/open_metrics_spec/#metricpoint-1) rule, i.e. expose classic histogram series ungrouped (for example alphabetically sorted: all `_bucket` lines, then all `_count`, then all `_sum`). NHCBParser is streaming and expects all classic histogram series (`_bucket`, `_count`, `_sum`) for a single label set to appear contiguously (see [`processClassicHistogramSeries`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/3abd048b685ef47889706be2e446fb2e4552c1f5/model/textparse/nhcbparse.go)) When the label set changes, it prematurely emits incomplete NHCB histograms: bucket-only histograms with `Sum: 0`, duplicate count-only histograms with empty `CustomValues`, and the trailing `_sum` lines get dropped by `TempHistogram.Convert`. Such ungrouped ordering is technically allowed by the Prometheus text format (<https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats/#grouping-and-sorting> only requires one group per metric family and increasing `le` order), whereas OpenMetrics 1.0 forbids interleaving Metrics and MetricPoints within a MetricFamily (<https://prometheus.io/docs/specs/om/open_metrics_spec/#metric-1>, <https://prometheus.io/docs/specs/om/open_metrics_spec/#metricpoint-1>). This is a known issue. We could fix it, but it would add overhead for a niche case (e.g. Kong used to expose metrics this way but has since fixed it), so this PR only pins down the current behaviour. ```release-notes NONE ```

content: @bboreham [wrote](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/19165#pullrequestreview-4959750511): > I am not sure that counting computed subquery samples the same as raw samples is correct. I would also like to question this - if we are going to count the computed sample from a subquery, then we should also do the same for range vector selectors. eg. let's say we're evaluating an instant query. If the subquery in `max_over_time(foo[1h:5m]))` produces 12 samples, then with this PR we'd return 13 total samples (12 samples processed in subquery + 1 sample returned from `max_over_time`). However, if the range vector selector in `max_over_time(foo[1h])` produces 12 samples, then we'd still only return 12 total samples, because the sample returned from `max_over_time` is not counted in this case. For consistency, I think both cases should be handled the same - either the computed sample from the function over the range vector (subquery or selector) should always be counted or never counted. My 2c is to not count the computed sample given we don't count samples computed by other operations like aggregations, but I don't hold this opinion strongly.

author: DanCech
content: promql: count subquery samples in total sample stats ## Summary Count the samples processed by a subquery's inner evaluation in the parent query's `TotalSamples` / `TotalSamplesPerStep` statistics, and make `TotalSamples` and `SamplesRead` agree on which subquery steps the parent consumes. - **`MergeTotalSamplesFromSubquery`** is new: both subquery call sites in the engine now merge the child's total-sample stats into the parent, in addition to the peak and samples-read stats they already absorbed. - **`SubqueryConsumer`** describes how the parent consumes a subquery (step grid, offset, window range, `@` timestamp). Both merges take it and use the same rule for which child steps are consumed. - **`@` subqueries in range queries** now report the same per-step stats as the equivalent instant query, for both `TotalSamples` and `SamplesRead`. ## Problem `evalSubquery` previously merged only `PeakSamples` and `SamplesRead` from a subquery child into the parent. `TotalSamples` was intentionally skipped on the assumption that the outer range-vector caller re-counts the materialized matrix. As a result the work done inside the subquery -- the samples its inner query processes to produce each step -- was never reflected in `TotalSamples`, so subquery-backed range evaluations under-reported the samples they consumed. The undercounting grows with nesting. Two new test cases in `promql/engine_test.go` show the effect: - `sum_over_time(metricWith1SampleEvery10Seconds[60s])` on its own reports `TotalSamples: 24` (6 samples per 60s window * 4 steps). - Wrapping that exact expression in a `[10s:10s]` subquery, `last_over_time(sum_over_time(metricWith1SampleEvery10Seconds[60s])[10s:10s])`, used to report only the 4 materialized points and drop the 24 samples of real work the inner query still performs. With the fix it reports `TotalSamples: 28` (24 inner input samples + 4 materialized points). The doubly-nested case `sum_over_time(max_over_time(metricWith3SampleEvery10Seconds[60s] @ 300)[5m:1m] @ 600)[10m:2m]` is more extreme: `TotalSamples` goes from `75` to `525`, a 7x correction, because each layer's inner work was previously discarded. Separately, `SamplesRead` dropped all subquery reads for a subquery with `@` in a range query: the child's timestamps sit around the `@` time, before the parent's first window, so the gap filter discarded them. `quantile_over_time(time() / 1000, metric[20s:10s] @ 200)` from 250s to 280s reported `SamplesRead: 0`, while the instant query at 250s reports 2. ## Solution A parent step at `parentTs` consumes the child steps whose timestamps, shifted by the subquery's original offset, fall in `(parentTs - range, parentTs]`. Child steps outside every window are not counted by either metric. - **`TotalSamples`** counts every child step in each parent step's window, so overlapping windows count a child step once per window, matching how range-vector functions count their window at every step. Parent windows only move forward, so the merge slides over the child steps and is linear in the number of parent and child steps. - **`SamplesRead`** counts each consumed child step once, at the earliest parent step that consumes it. - **With `@`**, every parent step consumes the fixed window `(atTs - range, atTs]`. Totals charge that window at every step; reads are counted once at the first step. - **Instant queries** fold the child's totals into the single step. For `@` subqueries in range queries, the child is still evaluated past the `@` window, so the range query's `PeakSamples` is higher than the instant query's (19 vs 7 in the new test). author: vpranckaitis
content: IIUC, this is being added for the functionality of `ProjectionLabels`, right? I also though about such feature a while ago. In my opinion, while using whole series hash as a substitution for removed labels might work in majority of cases, it could cause divergence from normal behavior in a few particular cases, which could limit the applicability of the feature. This might happen if some parts of the query would destroy distinguishing dimensions. For example, let's say we have these two timeseries: ``` some_series{instance="a", type="1"} some_series{instance="b", type="1"} ``` If we had query like this ``` sum by (instance) (label_replace(some_series, "instance", "_", "instance", ".*")) ``` without any label projection, you should get an error `vector cannot contain metrics with the same labelset` after `label_replace()` destroys the distinguishing dimension. Now if we implemented label projection, but we substituted removed labels with a series hash, the intermediate representation of series would look something like this: ``` {instance="a", __series_hash__="123"} {instance="b", __series_hash__="456"} ``` When running this through the same query, you wouldn't get the `vector cannot contain metrics with the same labelset` error anymore, because the series would still differ due to `__series_hash__` dimension. A better approach might be to use a hash of removed labels. Then, if those removed labels weren't sufficient to distinguish timeseries, you could still catch the moment when series end up with duplicated labelsets. E.g., the intermediate representation could look something like: ``` {instance="a", __removed_labels_hash__="123"} {instance="b", __removed_labels_hash__="123"} ``` Then we could catch the duplication of timeseries after destroying the distinguishing dimension of `instance` label. While this example with `label_replace()` is a bit contrived, I believe something similar might happen with functions that remove the metric name (unless delayed name removal is enabled), if you fetch timeseries with multiple names e.g. `{__name__=~"request_success|request_failure"}`. And while this PR doesn't add synthetic labels, but introduce `OriginalLabelsHash()` method instead, I think the same issue of series hash vs removed label hash might still hold, doesn't it?

author: GiedriusS
content: If I understood your comment correctly, in my $privatefork of thanos-io/promql-engine I avoided this issue by making the engine aware of the OriginalLabelsHash() method instead of basing it all on just labels. I know that it is very nice for long-term maintenance when there are just very few models to maintain e.g. everything is a label but overall I got quite a huge efficiency gain by not putting the hash into a label. Thanos has to dedup across millions of series and it is much faster when you just get a hash as an integer value instead of having it to decode again. It was already stored as an uint64 (right now) on the storage layer so I would love not to encode/decode. Finally, storing a binary value as a string wastes bytes: https://blog.kevinalbs.com/base122

author: serhiy-bzhezytskyy
content: otlptranslator: keep le="+Inf" equal to count when a bound is +Inf The OTel Go SDK accepts `+Inf` as an explicit bucket boundary: `AggregationExplicitBucketHistogram.err()` validates only that the boundaries are monotonic, so `Boundaries{1, 2, math.Inf(1)}` is accepted, and recording through it emits `explicit_bounds = [1 2 +Inf]` with `bucket_counts = [5 2 3 0]`. The trailing bucket spans `(+Inf, +infinity)`, so it cannot hold an observation. On input of that shape this path emits `le="+Inf"` twice for the same series and timestamp: once from the loop over explicit bounds, carrying the running sum at that bound, and once synthesized from `pt.Count()`. Both samples are written. The two values are equal whenever `count` equals the sum of the bucket counts below the bound, which the producible shape satisfies, so the defect there is the duplicate write alone; they diverge only when the data point violates the sum rule as well, either through a non-empty trailing bucket or a `count` that is not the sum of `bucket_counts`. The change skips an infinite bound in the loop, lets the synthesized bucket carry the count, and reports the bound: ```go if math.IsInf(bound, 1) { c.plusInfAnnots.Add(newCategorizedWarningf(WarningCategoryHistogramPlusInfBound, "histogram data point has an explicit +Inf bound, le=\"+Inf\" is taken from count")) continue } ``` `explicit_bounds` is required to be strictly increasing, so `+Inf` is the last bound and no later bucket depends on the skipped iteration; its own count is already added to the running sum before the guard. The bound's exemplars still reach the synthesized bucket through the remainder assigned after the loop, so no exemplar is dropped. No pre-existing fixture in the package set an infinite bound, so the guard changes no output that was already covered. The NHCB path already refuses this input: `checkHistogramCustomBounds` rejects an explicitly defined `+Inf` bound in `model/histogram/generic.go`, reached from `Histogram.Validate`, and #17320 kept that while relaxing `-Inf`. Repairing it silently here was inconsistent with that, hence the warning, in the same category style as `histogram_zero_count_non_zero_sum`. It is merged into the annotations `FromMetrics` returns, and deduplicated by message, so a translation reports it once however many data points carry the bound. `TestPrometheusConverter_AddHistogramDataPoints` covers three shapes: the one a producer emits, and two that are invalid in different ways, a non-empty trailing bucket and a `count` above the bucket sum. All three fail without the guard. #### Which issue(s) does the PR fix: Fixes #19424 #### Release notes for end users (**ALL** commits must be considered). *Reviewers should verify clarity and quality.* ```release-notes [BUGFIX] OTLP: Do not emit `le="+Inf"` twice when a histogram's explicit bounds end at `+Inf`, and warn about the bound. ```

content: promql/parser: parenthesise a signed left operand of ^ #### Which issue(s) does the PR fix: None filed. `^` binds tighter than a unary sign, but the printer wrote a signed left operand of `^` without parentheses. In parsed queries this happens with `Inf`, which prints as `+Inf`. So `inf ^ 2` printed as `+Inf ^ 2`, which parses back as `+(Inf ^ 2)` and prints as `++Inf ^ 2` the next time. In ASTs built in code, the sign changes the result: a `BinaryExpr` of `-2 ^ 2` printed as `-2 ^ 2`, which evaluates to -4, not 4. `String()` and `Pretty()` now put such an operand in parentheses, as `(+Inf) ^ 2`. Everywhere else, `+Inf` is still spelled the same. The web UI serializes number literals separately (`translate_ast.go` and `serialize.ts`). Its version of this fix is in #19823. Not changed: `DurationExpr` prints `^` without the same check, which only matters for ASTs built in code. #### Release notes for end users (**ALL** commits must be considered). ```release-notes [BUGFIX] PromQL: Put a signed left operand of `^` in parentheses when printing a query, so that `inf ^ 2` no longer prints as `+Inf ^ 2`. ```

content:
{"body":"Reviewed the whole change against the current ApplyConfig/egisterProviders flow (CI is green across the board).

**What checks out**

- **Mechanism label.** Refresh series are labelled with the mechanism the discoverer actually passes (Mech: "ec2"/"ecs"/"rds"/"lightsail"/"elasticache"/"msk" in discovery/aws), while (*SDConfig).Name() returns "aws". So the old DeleteLabelValues(cfg.Name(), sub) was a silent no-op for AWS, and RefreshMechanism() returning string(c.Role) matches the Role enum exactly (RoleEC2 = "ec2", ...). I checked every SD package that sets Mech: — AWS is the only one where mech != Name(), so the opt-in interface needs just this one override.
- **Ordering.** egisterProviders runs before the cancel loop and m.providers = newProviders is assigned before the cleanup loops, so deleteRefreshMetrics sees both surviving *and* freshly-added providers (the "job changes to another job's config" case depends on that). ApplyConfig also holds m.mtx for its whole body, so the unlocked reads of p.setName/p.config in deleteRefreshMetrics are race-free.
- **Value preservation.** Instantiate is just WithLabelValues, so in the headline case (same job, changed url) the successor provider resolves to the *same* child and the counters survive. On rename the tomic.Pointer swap means an in-flight efresh() can only write into a handle that has just been deleted — such a write never re-enters the vec's children map, so there is no resurrected series.
- **Guard symmetry.** enamed[prov] is recorded only inside the setNameUpdater check, i.e. exactly when UpdateSetName ran, so we never delete for a rename that didn't happen.

**Suggestions**

1. Doc comments don't match their identifiers: `// DeleteRefreshMetrics deletes ...` sits on `func (m *Manager) deleteRefreshMetrics`, and `// SetName is the name of ...` on the `setName` field.
2. Release note only covers half the change. On AWS, `DeleteLabelValues("aws", sub)` never matched, so refresh series for removed AWS jobs survived every reload — this PR is what actually removes them. Suggest a second line, e.g. `[BUGFIX] Discovery: Remove stale aws_sd refresh metrics on reload; they were kept because the mechanism label is the role, not the config name.` (which is the fa9748d commit's effect).
3. Test gap: a provider shared by two subs (`{A, B}`, `setName = A`) where **B** is dropped. Nothing should be deleted and the `config` label must remain `A` — the table only covers removal of the `setName` sub itself, not of a sibling sub.
4. In the rename case the series changes identity (`config="old"` -> `config="new"`) and the new series starts at 0. Correct, but the PR body's "the series would stay on reload" reads as if values persist; one clarifying sentence would prevent someone reporting the reset as a regression.
5. Pre-existing, not introduced here: `prometheus_sd_refresh_duration_histogram_seconds` is labelled `mechanism` only and is never deleted, so it outlives all providers of that mechanism. Fine to leave for a follow-up.

author: bwplotka
content: storage: resolve classic and NHCB histogram collisions in NHCBAsClassicQuerier > [!NOTE] > This is chained with https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18048, marking as draft until we merge that one. Addresses <https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18048#discussion_r4145645412> by resolving collisions between stored classic histograms and converted NHCB series in `NHCBAsClassicQuerier`: - Group stored classic and NHCB series by histogram identity (labels excluding `__name__` and `le`) when both representations exist for the queried metric, while keeping the pure-classic and pure-NHCB paths streaming. - At timestamps where a stored classic histogram has a live sample, shadow converted NHCB samples across the entire histogram group so that differences in bucket layouts or `le` formatting (e.g. `"1"` vs OpenMetrics `"1.0"`) do not produce duplicate or hybrid buckets. - Merge disjoint time ranges across a classic $\leftrightarrow$ NHCB migration cutover into a single continuous `Series`, preferring live samples over `StaleNaN` at the cutover timestamp and dropping delayed staleness markers from the old representation after the new representation is active. - Propagate `StaleNaN` onto active converted classic series when an NHCB series emits a staleness marker, when a custom bucket boundary is removed on a subsequent NHCB sample, when the series transitions to an exponential native histogram, or when a stored classic histogram takes over after NHCB samples. - Only trigger NHCB conversion when the query has an equality `__name__` matcher (`MatchEqual`), apply all `le` matchers, and ignore base series that already carry an explicit `le` label. - Sort output series by `labels.Compare` (per group when `sortSeries=false`, and globally across groups when `sortSeries=true` for `NewMergeQuerier` / `remote_read`). ### Streaming & Buffering Behavior After peeking a single element (`firstNHCB` / `firstClassic`) from each `SeriesSet` in `NHCBAsClassicQuerier.Select` (<https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/317bd37c0162f69937a68f420fbdac5f51a6127e/storage/nhcb_querier.go#L72-L209>), the querier takes one of four paths: | Query Scenario | `SeriesSet` Streaming | Sample Materialization | Why | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 1. Pure classic (`firstNHCB == nil`) | 100% streaming (`classicSet` returned directly) | 100% streaming (zero sample buffering) | Preserves `le` index pushdown and returns the underlying TSDB `SeriesSet` untouched. | | 2. Pure NHCB (`firstClassic == nil`, `sortSeries == false` or `_count`/`_sum`) | 100% streaming per NHCB series (`nhcbSet.Next()` pulled lazily in `nhcbToClassicSeriesSet.Next`: <https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/317bd37c0162f69937a68f420fbdac5f51a6127e/storage/nhcb_querier.go#L467-L506>) | 1 NHCB series at a time (slab lives only until the next NHCB series is pulled) | For `_count`/`_sum`, converting `foo` to `foo_count`/`foo_sum` adds no `le` label, so streaming 1-by-1 preserves global `labels.Compare` order even when `sortSeries == true`. For `_bucket` (`sortSeries == false`, which is all local PromQL evaluation), each NHCB series expands into its $B+1$ bucket series on demand. | | 3. Hybrid / colliding metric (`firstClassic != nil && firstNHCB != nil`, `sortSeries == false`) | Grouped by `Series` ref at `Select`, converted 1 group at a time on `Next()` | 1 histogram group at a time | `classicSet` and `nhcbSet` cannot be co-streamed in lockstep without `histogramIndex` (<https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/317bd37c0162f69937a68f420fbdac5f51a6127e/storage/nhcb_querier.go#L233-L273>): when `sortSeries == false`, TSDB iterates in internal series-ref order; even with `sortSeries == true`, classic `_bucket` series have a `"le"` label (`"le"` sorts before any label name `> "le"` like `method`, `pod`, `service`, `status`, `zone`), so buckets of the same histogram (`{le="+Inf", method="GET"}` and `{le="0.5", method="GET"}`) are separated by `{le="+Inf", method="POST"}` in `labels.Compare` order. `histogramIndex` only indexes `storage.Series` pointers; sample iterators are decoded lazily when `Next()` reaches that group. | | 4. `sortSeries == true` on `_bucket` (used by `NewMergeQuerier` with `remote_read`) | Materialized & sorted across groups | Materialized across groups | Because `"le"` sorts before label names `> "le"`, global `labels.Compare` order across multiple NHCB series interleaves buckets from different NHCB series and requires sorting converted bucket series before yielding. | Unlike classic histograms where `le` is in the TSDB index, an NHCB series stores custom bucket boundaries (`CustomValues`) inside its encoded histogram chunks. Decoding the NHCB series once into its $B+1$ bucket series discovers the `le` values required by `Series.Labels()` and avoids decoding the same NHCB chunk $B+1$ times when PromQL iterates each bucket series. ### Benchmarks vs. PR #18048 (`1,000` NHCB series $\times$ `30` custom buckets = `31,000` bucket series, `6` samples/series) ``` name old time/op new time/op delta NHCBAsClassicSelect_Bucket-24 82.3ms ± 2% 29.4ms ± 3% -64.28% NHCBAsClassicSelect_Count-24 3.78ms ± 2% 2.19ms ± 2% -42.06% NHCBAsClassicSelect_Sum-24 3.77ms ± 1% 2.19ms ± 1% -41.91% name old alloc/op new alloc/op delta NHCBAsClassicSelect_Bucket-24 34.3MB ± 0% 11.5MB ± 0% -66.62% NHCBAsClassicSelect_Count-24 957kB ± 0% 354kB ± 0% -63.04% NHCBAsClassicSelect_Sum-24 957kB ± 0% 354kB ± 0% -63.04% name old allocs/op new allocs/op delta NHCBAsClassicSelect_Bucket-24 565k ± 0% 33k ± 0% -94.13% NHCBAsClassicSelect_Count-24 18.1k ± 0% 3.0k ± 0% -83.27% NHCBAsClassicSelect_Sum-24 18.1k ± 0% 3.0k ± 0% -83.27% ``` ```release-notes NONE ```

content: promql: handle empty input in BucketFraction Fixes #19943 The exported `BucketFraction` helper panics with `index out of range [-1]` for a nil or empty bucket slice: it reads `buckets[len(buckets)-1]` to check for a `+Inf` last bucket before any length check. Return `NaN` for nil and empty slices, mirroring the `BucketQuantile` fix in #19927 (this is the follow-up @krajorama asked for there) and the native-histogram counterpart's zero-observation behavior. `NaN` is also what `BucketFraction` already returns for a nonempty slice whose last bucket is not `+Inf` and for a zero total count, so no new semantics are introduced. This corrects an internal exported-helper contract; the current PromQL call site in `funcHistogramFraction` guards empty bucket lists before calling the helper, so no expression-evaluation failure is claimed. Verification: - The reporter's repro (`BucketFraction(0, 1, nil)`) panics on pristine `main` (39c878f) at `promql/quantile.go:544` and returns `NaN` with this change. - New `TestBucketFraction_EmptyBuckets` covers nil and non-nil empty slices across finite, reversed, infinite, and NaN bounds (all `NaN`), with a zero-count `+Inf` control; it panics with only the production change reverted and passes with it restored. A small `TestBucketFraction` control pins existing nonempty behavior (interpolated fraction, full range, reversed bounds). - Full `go test ./promql` passes; `gofmt` clean. ```release-notes NONE ``` Developed with AI assistance.

author: EgorKhaklin
content: promql/parser: allow the expanding notation on Inf, NaN and stale #### Which issue(s) does the PR fix: None filed. In a series description, `1x3` and `_x3` expand, but `NaNx3`, `Infx3` and `stalex3` fail with `unexpected identifier "NaNx3" in series values, expected number or "stale"`: the lexer reads the word and the `x3` after it as one identifier. The grammar already has `series_value TIMES uint` for these values; the lexer never lets them reach it. A series value word (`Inf`, `NaN`, `stale`) now stops before a directly following `x`, as `lexNumber` already stops a number there (`l.seriesDesc && r == 'x'`). Every other word is lexed as before (`maxx2` stays one identifier), and `stale` stays case-sensitive as the grammar requires. Found while writing promtool unit tests for [Polaris](https://github.com/EgorKhaklin/polaris-id)'s alert rules, where a gauge reads NaN when it could not be measured. Tests: lexer cases for `NaNx2 -Infx1 stalex3` and an unchanged `maxx2`; a `TestParseSeries` case for `Infx2 -Infx1`; a new test for `NaNx2` and `stalex2`, whose values `require.Equal` cannot compare. All three fail without the lexer change. `go test ./promql/parser/... ./cmd/promtool/` pass. A rule test using `NaNx4` and `stalex3` passes with this branch's promtool and fails with the released one. One example added to `unit_testing_rules.md`. #### Release notes for end users (**ALL** commits must be considered). *Reviewers should verify clarity and quality.* ```release-notes [ENHANCEMENT] promtool: The expanding notation `axn` works on `Inf`, `NaN` and `stale` in test series values, as in `stalex3`. ```

content: promql: preserve quantile bucket for histograms with NaN sum When a native histogram's sum is NaN, `HistogramQuantile` scans the remaining buckets to determine whether to report NaN observations. That scan overwrote the selected bucket, causing interpolation to use the last bucket instead. Preserve the selected bucket while accumulating the remaining counts. For observations `{1.5, 3, NaN}`, `histogram_quantile(0.2, …)` returned approximately `3.0314` instead of `1.5157`. Add regression tests for multiple populated buckets, a no-NaN control, and a NaN sum caused by observing both `-Inf` and `+Inf`. The three bug cases fail without the fix; the control passes either way. Validation: lint, race-enabled Go tests, generated parser check, and UI tests/lint passed. #### Which issue(s) does the PR fix: None. #### Release notes for end users (**ALL** commits must be considered). ```release-notes [BUGFIX] PromQL: Fix `histogram_quantile` and `histogram_quantiles` interpolating within the wrong bucket for native histograms whose sum is NaN. ```

content: ui/codemirror-promql: quote UTF-8 names in autocomplete and flag unquoted ones Quote UTF-8 metric and label names in the PromQL editor. - Accepting an autocomplete suggestion for a metric name, label name or label value that needs quoting now inserts it quoted. A quoted metric name is moved inside the braces next to the existing matchers (`foo{a="b"}` -> `{"foo.bar", a="b"}`). - Names typed without quotes (`foo.bar`, `métrique`) are still completed, and the completion adds the quotes. - Completion inside quoted names (`{"fo|"}`, `by ("a|")`, `{"a|"="x"}`) now works, and offers label names as well as metric names where either is valid. - Unquoted UTF-8 names are reported by the linter (`name must be quoted: "foo.bar"`) and the rest of the name is highlighted as invalid. - Selectors sent to the API (`match[]`) quote names and escape values, and the label values path uses the `U__` escaping. - Quoted names and values are unescaped when parsed. - Quoted label names in `on(...)`, `ignoring(...)`, `group_left(...)` and `group_right(...)` are taken into account by the vector matching checks (for example the "label must not occur in ON and GROUP clause at once" diagnostic). - Quoted label names are highlighted as label names, and a quoted metric name as a metric name, instead of as strings. - A quoted metric name is not repeated as a `__name__` matcher in the selectors sent to the API. - `escapePromQLString` moved from `complete/hybrid.ts` to `parser/utf8.ts`, and now also escapes `\n`, `\r` and `\t`, so label values containing them are inserted as valid string literals. Known limitation: the leading ASCII part of an unquoted name (`foo` in `foo.bar`) keeps its normal highlighting, as the lezer tokenizer only knows legacy identifiers. The whole name is still underlined by the linter. #### Which issue(s) does the PR fix: Fixes #15236 Fixes #15202 #### Release notes for end users (**ALL** commits must be considered). *Reviewers should verify clarity and quality.* ```release-notes [ENHANCEMENT] UI: Quote UTF-8 metric and label names in editor autocompletion, and flag unquoted UTF-8 names as errors. ```
